title: The step tau_{<=q-1}K -> tau_{<=q}K of canonical truncations: short exact sequence and quasi-isomorphism of the cokernel to H^q(K)[-q]
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category and $K$ a cochain complex of $\mathcal A$ with differentials $d^r:K^r\to K^{r+1}$ and cohomology $H^r(K)=\Ker d^r/\Im d^{r-1}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $q\in\mathbf Z$ let $\tau_{\leq q}K$ be the subcomplex $\cdots\to K^{q-2}\to K^{q-1}\to\Ker(d^q)\to0\to\cdots$ of $K$ (so $(\tau_{\leq q}K)^r=K^r$ for $r<q$, $=\Ker d^q$ for $r=q$, $=0$ for $r>q$), and let $H^q(K)[-q]$ be the complex with $H^q(K)$ in degree $q$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then:
(a) $\tau_{\leq q-1}K$ is a subcomplex of $\tau_{\leq q}K$; the inclusion $i_q$ is a monomorphism of complexes, and its cokernel $M_q(K)=\tau_{\leq q}K/\tau_{\leq q-1}K$ (formed degreewise) is the complex with $M_q(K)^{q-1}=K^{q-1}/\Ker d^{q-1}$, $M_q(K)^q=\Ker d^q$, differential $M_q(K)^{q-1}\to M_q(K)^q$ induced by $d^{q-1}$, and $0$ in all other degrees; thus $0\to\tau_{\leq q-1}K\xrightarrow{i_q}\tau_{\leq q}K\xrightarrow{p_q}M_q(K)\to0$ is a short exact sequence of complexes ($p_q$ the quotient map).
(b) The morphism of complexes $j_q:\tau_{\leq q}K\to H^q(K)[-q]$ that is the projection $\Ker d^q\to H^q(K)$ in degree $q$ and $0$ elsewhere factors uniquely as $j_q=\bar j_q\circ p_q$, and $\bar j_q:M_q(K)\to H^q(K)[-q]$ (the projection $\Ker d^q\to H^q(K)$ in degree $q$) is a quasi-isomorphism: $H^{q-1}(M_q(K))=0$ because $K^{q-1}/\Ker d^{q-1}\to\Ker d^q$ is a monomorphism, and $H^q(\bar j_q)$ is the identity of $\Ker d^q/\Im d^{q-1}=H^q(K)$.
(c) Everything is natural in $K$: a morphism of complexes $f:K\to L$ restricts to morphisms $\tau_{\leq q}f$, $\tau_{\leq q-1}f$, induces $M_q(f)$, and $(\tau_{\leq q-1}f,\tau_{\leq q}f,M_q(f))$ is a morphism of short exact sequences with $H^q(f)[-q]\circ\bar j_q=\bar j_q\circ M_q(f)$.

proof.text: Construct the step inclusion by inv(iota_q of truncLE(q-1) K) followed by truncLEMap(iota_(q-1), q). The inner inclusion is an isomorphism since truncLE(q-1) K is strictly supported at most q. Truncation naturality gives compatibility into K. This makes the step inclusion mono because its composite into K is mono. The cokernel sequence of a mono in an abelian category is short exact. These are the proved private helpers stepInclusion, stepInclusion_comp, stepInclusion_mono, stepInclusion_shortExact.

Identify the q-th truncation term with cycles and its inclusion with iCycles, using the opposite-category truncation formulas and the cycles/opcycles isomorphism. Cancel iCycles in the chain-map equation to show that the incoming truncation differential followed by this identification is iota in the preceding degree followed by toCycles. Since toCycles followed by homology projection is zero, mkHomToSingle constructs the projection. Its q-th component has the required normalization; the other components vanish. The composite of the step inclusion with this projection is zero: its source in degree q is zero and the target in other degrees is zero.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-upper-step-quotient-coordinates] to the constructed inclusion and its proved compatibility. Obtain the support, e0 and e1, the projection and differential equations, and monicity of the quotient differential.

Define barj by cokernel.desc of the constructed projection and its proved annihilation. The cokernel equation gives the factorization. Cancel the epi cokernel projection to prove uniqueness. At q its component is epi; cancel it after composing with e1 to derive the required normalization for barj from that for the projection and the projection equation for e1.

In degree q-1 use zero support in degree q-2 and the mono quotient differential: ShortComplex.exact_iff_mono gives exactness and hence zero homology. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-two-term-coimage-quasiiso] with the obtained coordinate isomorphisms, support, differential equation, monicity and the proved barj normalization. This gives the quasi-isomorphism.

Cancel the mono inclusion into L in truncation naturality to prove naturality of the step inclusion. To prove naturality of the projection, first cancel iCycles to establish naturality of the truncation cycles identification. Then use homology projection naturality at q; in other degrees the target term is zero. Define g by cokernel.map of the naturality square for the inclusions. Its projection equation is the universal-property equation of cokernel.map. Finally cancel the epi cokernel projection, use both factorization equations and projection naturality, to prove naturality of barj.

proof_origin.place: Remark 08J5, second truncation triangle, with the canonical constructions of Tag 0118. F2 implements inclusion, projection, descent, uniqueness, vanishing and naturality in Lean; quotient coordinates and two-term quasi-isomorphism are split into two named nodes.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (checked against Stacks homology.tex Tag 0118 and derived.tex Remark 08J5; Stacks only says 'in a similar way', so the degreewise computation is written out). Proof in 7 steps: the inclusion i_q (degreewise, elementary); the complex M_q(K) with differential delta: K^{q-1}/Ker d^{q-1} -> Ker d^q, a monomorphism with image Im d^{q-1} (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-coimage-mono, Abelian.factorThruCoimage is mono); p_q a morphism of complexes with p_q i_q = 0; clause (a) by degreewise short exactness and the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact (Stacks 0114; HomologicalComplex.instAbelian, shortExact_iff_degreewise_shortExact, ShortExact.gIsCokernel), which also gives p_q a cokernel of i_q and epi; clause (b) factorization (uniqueness from p_q epi) and the quasi-isomorphism by computing H^{q-1}(M_q)=0, H^q(M_q)=H^q(K); clause (c) naturality degreewise. Not a Mathlib leaf: Mathlib has the sequence truncLE n K -> K -> X3 for the inclusion into K, but no step truncLE (q-1) K -> truncLE q K and no identification of the quotient with the single complex of H^q(K) (searched with LeanSearch, LeanFinder and grep; Loogle was rate-limited for the item, its earlier LeanFinder/grep records stand).
